31.name: Sink or Swim - Michael Klim
31.overview: Six years ago, Olympic champion Michael Klim almost lost the ability to walk. Then he received a devastating diagnosis. In this moving episode, Klim reveals how he hit rock bottom but ultimately emerged stronger.

31.name: Finding Alby Mangels
31.overview: The reclusive adventure filmmaker and '80s icon Alby Mangels looks back on an extraordinary career and explains why he turned his back on fame.

31.name: Out in the Open - Sophie Hyde
31.overview: Sophie Hyde is one of Australia's most successful directors, working with some of Hollywood's finest. But in her latest film she turns the spotlight on her own family.

31.name: Nabbed - Ian Williams
31.overview: When pensioner Ian Williams lost $1,300 in a banking scam, he expected a quick refund and apology. The bank's response so incensed the "stubborn bugger", he sued it for $379,000,000.

31.name: Raising Richard - Deirdre Croft
31.overview: Who cares for our children when we're gone if they can't care for themselves? As Deirdre Croft faces the end of her life, she's on a mission to ensure her son is looked after when she's gone.

31.name: Morning Star - Witiyana Marika
31.overview: From Arnhem Land to rock stardom, Yothu Yindi's Witiyana Marika was destined to take centre stage. Now, at a crucial time for his community, he's shed his dreadlocks and emerged as a leader of his people.

31.name: What Doesn't Kill You - Ghanim Al Shnen
31.overview: Many would have despaired after losing both their arms but Ghanim Al Shnen embraced the possibilities of bionic medicine and focused on a dream - to be reunited with his family after 12 years apart.

31.name: The Leyland Brother - Mal Leyland
31.overview: In the 1960s and 70s, Mal Leyland was one of the best-known people on TV, as one half of the Leyland Brothers. Now at age 81, the pioneer of outback documentaries is suffering dementia - but still planning one last trip.

31.name: The Westall UFO Mystery
31.overview: In 1966, a Melbourne high school was thrown into chaos when strange objects appeared in the sky. Sixty years on from Australia's biggest UFO sighting, witnesses are still looking for answers about what they saw at Westall.

31.name: Lost - Celine Cremer (Part 1)
31.overview: Belgian backpacker Celine Cremer was on the trip of a lifetime but on a hike in Tasmania she took a wrong turn and was never seen again. More than two years later a group of friends and volunteers set out looking for answers.

31.name: Lost - Celine Cremer (Part 2)
31.overview: Two and half years after Belgian backpacker Celine Cremer went missing on a short hike, friends and local volunteers scour the forest and finally find the answers they're looking for.

31.name: A Year of Living Gratefully - James Valentine
31.overview: Broadcaster James Valentine was offered two different treatments for his cancer so he chose the one that let him keep doing what he loved. When it returned a year later, he faced the end with courage, purpose and humour.

31.name: The Hustler - John Polson
31.overview: John Polson was a troubled teen when a sliding doors moment led him into the world of acting. He went on to create Tropfest, one of the world's biggest short film festivals, changing his life and the Australian industry.

31.name: An Accidental Leader - Rob Armstrong
31.overview: Sheep farmer Rob Armstrong never expected to be the face of political resistance. But when his state government proposed a levy that would hit volunteer country firefighters, a childhood trauma propelled him into action.

31.name: Regeneration - Rachel Ward
31.overview: When Instagram trolls accused actor and director Rachel Ward of 'letting herself go', she used the attention to talk about her passion, regenerative farming, which has given her a renewed sense of purpose.

31.name: A Seat At The Table - Mohamed Semra
31.overview: At 15, Mohamed Semra made headlines when he was kicked out of a Melbourne Apple Store by staff who were worried he might steal something. At 27, he's making history as the first Australian mayor from sub-Saharan Africa.

31.name: Down to the Wire - Saul Griffith
31.overview: When Australian Story first met inventor Saul Griffith in 2023 he was on a mission to electrify the world. Although political changes in the US have tested his optimism, back home his own community is forging ahead.

31.name: A Beautiful Mind - Richard Scolyer
31.overview: When Richard Scolyer was diagnosed with brain cancer three years ago, he volunteered to undergo risky, new treatment, hoping for a medical breakthrough. As we filmed in his final months, he reflects on his life and legacy.

31.name: Child's Play - 60 Years of Play School
31.overview: Australia's shared family heirloom Play School is celebrating 60 years on air, but what's the secret to its enduring success? With rare behind-the-scenes access, Australian Story examines its creative process with insights from past and present cast and crew.

31.name: His Brilliant Careers - Sam Neill
31.overview: As a tribute to the late Sam Neill, we look back over the actor's dazzling career and recent health struggles.

31.name: Sky's The Limit
31.overview: On a cold June night, a group of Jewish friends gathered at Melbourne airport to welcome a Muslim family they'd never met. One year later, they share their story of friendship and hope across religious and cultural divides.

31.name: Turning The Page - Luke Bateman
31.overview: Luke Bateman was flying high as an NRL player until a devastating gambling addiction destroyed his career. Saved by his love of books, he's now writing fantasy novels and says he's never been happier.

31.name: Blood On The Tracks (Update)
31.overview: When teenager Mark Haines was discovered dead on train tracks near the NSW town of Tamworth, his uncle was convinced it was foul play. Almost four decades later, a new inquest reveals fresh evidence and a cover-up.

31.name: Bad Blood - Tristan Stanley
31.overview: The 1980s contaminated blood crisis devastated the lives of thousands of Australians who became infected with Hep C or HIV. Now survivor Tristan Stanley is heading a last-ditch campaign seeking justice for those left behind.

31.name: The Final Act
31.overview: When dancer Roz Hervey was diagnosed with motor neurone disease, her daughter, actor Tilda Cobham-Hervey, stepped behind the camera to record her mother's life story. With hours left to live, Roz made a dying wish.

31.name: Unleashed - Barnaby Joyce
31.overview: Barnaby Joyce's defection to One Nation struck some as opportunism, others as evidence of an unrivalled political radar. But is the party big enough for him and Pauline Hanson?

31.name: Australian Story: Celebrating 30 Years
31.overview: A special 70-minute episode celebrating 30 years of Australian Story. Leigh Sales hosts a live extravaganza at the Sydney Opera House featuring past guests and musical acts.

31.name: Time After Time - Cheng Lei
31.overview: Journalist Cheng Lei discovered that the trauma of being separated from her children for three years didn't end with her release from a Chinese prison.

31.name: The Girl Next Door - Molly Ticehurst
31.overview: Molly Ticehurst's brutal murder at the hands of her ex-partner sparked outrage. Family and friends from the NSW town of Forbes reveal how the young mother did everything to save herself but the system let her down.

31.name: Eyes on the Prize - Kris Rallah-Baker
31.overview: Australia's first Indigenous eye surgeon Kris Rallah-Baker has walked a zigzag path, driven by family struggles and overcoming racism. Now he's on a mission to heal blindness and empower the next generation.

31.name: Wild - Chrissy Amphlett (Part 1)
31.overview: Divinyls lead singer Chrissy Amphlett was a rock icon who lived hard and burnt bright until her death at 53. Over two episodes featuring unseen footage, friends, family and bandmates reflect on her wild life and rich legacy.

31.name: Wild - Chrissy Amphlett (Part 2)
31.overview: In Part 2 on Divinyls singer Chrissy Amphlett, the band implodes, she falls in love and finds a new musical direction. But before her death, she records three songs with Tim Finn that have only now seen the light of day.

31.name: A Second Start - Katie Noonan
31.overview: In 2024, acclaimed singer Katie Noonan's life fell apart when she split with her husband. Her new album reflects the grief of separation but is tempered with lyrics about falling in love, gifted to her by writer Trent Dalton.

31.name: The Road Back
31.overview: It was one of Australia's deadliest bus crashes, killing 10 and injuring 25. Three years on from the Hunter Valley crash, survivors speak for the first time about the horror, their recovery and the need for systemic change.

overview: Putting the "real" back into reality television, Australian Story is an award-winning documentary series with no narrator and no agendas — just authentic stories told entirely in people's own words.

seasons.name: Series 2016
seasons.overview: Celebrating its 20th anniversary in 2016, Australian Story returns with more unique stories that provide an insight into Australian life with all its complexities and challenges.

seasons.overview: The power of the personal. Compelling stories about real people that illuminate, entertain and inspire. Presented by Leigh Sales.
